title: MENDNet: Just-in-time Fault Detection and Mitigation in AI Systems with Uncertainty Quantification and Multi-Exit Networks
problem: Hardware faults in AI accelerator memory alter pre-trained DNN parameters during inference, causing prediction errors. Existing fault detection and mitigation techniques either interrupt execution or introduce latency incompatible with just-in-time handling.
motivation: Ensuring AI accelerator reliability is critical for safety-critical and mission-critical applications vulnerable to transient faults.
method: MENDNet detects hardware faults by watching the neural network's confidence at multiple checkpoints—intermediate points where the network could provide an answer—rather than waiting for the final result. It uses an energy-based uncertainty metric (a math-based measure of prediction confidence) at each checkpoint. When confidence suddenly drops, the system knows a hardware fault has corrupted the data and automatically switches to an earlier checkpoint that's still reliable. This catches errors without stopping the system or adding major delays.
key_novelty: The core idea is detecting hardware faults by monitoring neural network confidence at multiple intermediate points, then automatically switching to earlier checkpoints to avoid errors without system disruption.
contributions: Uncertainty quantification framework for efficient JIT fault detection without execution interruption
MENDNet system combining multi-exit networks with dynamic confidence thresholding for fault tolerance
Energy-based uncertainty metric for fault-aware early-exit selection
80.42% accuracy improvement over traditional DNN under fault injection
limitations: Specific limitations and scalability constraints not discussed in abstract.
